text:
maya: hey — noticing a huge skew on rollout `canary/v2-09`.
maya: intended weight 1% but observability shows ~24% of prod requests hitting canary in us-west-2 😬
maya: console: https://console.redwood/rollouts/canary/v2-09 (shows traffic by region)

deploy-bot: rollout canary/v2-09 updated by jordan at 1712356600 — target_weight=1% -> active

ojordan: I pushed a guard change earlier that switches header-affinity to use `X-Client-Id` instead of cookie when present.
ojordan: not aware of any mass-change that would bump weight, but will look.

sam: I repro'd a small test: when X-Client-Id contains a trailing suffix like `-stg` the proxy strip/normalize rules differ and the hash ends up in a different bucket.
sam: example (pseudo):
```
# canonical input used yesterday: "client-42:8080"
# after proxy change it's canonicalized -> "client-42"
hash("client-42:8080") % 100 != hash("client-42") % 100
```

lila: dashboard (rollouts -> inspector) shows cookie-affinity steady but header-affinity is all over the place for the same client segments.
lila: also seeing geo-concentration: mostly us-west hitting canary.

diego: digging — edge-proxy v2.7.0 rolled yesterday morning and added header canonicalization (lowercase + drop default ports). we relied on the raw header to include `:port` as part of salt previously.
diego: if salt/input to hashing changed, buckets will completely reshuffle -> explains the jump.

ojordan: ok that matches. two quick actions:
1) revert the proxy canonicalization for rollout paths (temp) to restore previous hashing behavior.
2) change rollout-service to compute bucket from a canonicalized, explicit field (e.g., `rollout_hash_input`) rather than relying on raw header value — and add a per-route salt that is stable.

maya: timeline? we should revert if it takes >30m to patch, to stop user impact.

diego: I can revert the proxy rules on the canary path now, rolling back in ~5m. will post deploy.

ojordan: I'll open a fix PR to rollout-service: use `concat(affinity_key, "|", route_salt)` and explicitly log the input in telemetry. PR + tests, then canary the change behind a feature flag.

deploy-bot: revert deploy started by diego at 1712356950 — canary path rule rollback in progress

diego: rollback finished. metrics already moving back toward expected distribution, will watch for 10m.

maya: thanks all. can we add an alert on large % delta vs target for a rollout weight? want auto-warning if actual_sent/target > 2x
lila: yes — filing telemetry ticket #3456 for rollout delta alert and another (#3457) for exposing the hash input in the inspector UI.

maya: perfect. :thumbsup:
